explanation: Woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island, off north-eastern Siberia, for centuries after the pyramid was built, dying out about 4,000 years ago. Mainland herds had vanished long before.

claims.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza was completed around 2560 BC.
The last known woolly mammoths, on Wrangel Island, died out about 4,000 years ago.
Wrangel Island lies in the Arctic Ocean off north-eastern Siberia.
Mainland woolly mammoth populations had died out long before the Wrangel Island population.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Great Pyramid of Giza: Sources place its completion in the early 25th century BCE, rather than at a single year near 2560 BC. It was built by Khufu (Cheops), the second king of Egypt's 4th dynasty (c. 2543–c. 2436 bce), and was completed in the early 25th century bce.

claimResults.note: The summary, drawing on Britannica's 'Great Pyramid of Giza', dates completion to the early 25th century BCE, not around 2560 BC. Other chronologies put Khufu at about 2589 to 2566 BC, which is where the familiar 2560 figure comes from. Sources disagree, so the label fails as written (§9.5.2). The comparison is safe under either chronology: both put the pyramid at least 450 years before the last mammoths (about 2000 BC). This call also serves p.nat.0173 and is counted here.

An examination of a fossil tooth discovered in 2015 indicated that a tiny population of mammoths persisted on Wrangel Island... as late as 4,300 years ago.
